function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick guide to help you find the best place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or just a convenient delivery option: | Category | What to Look For | Why It Matters | How to Find It | |----------|------------------|----------------|----------------| | **Local Bakery** | • Handmade, fresh‑baked cakes
• Custom designs & flavors
• Often uses seasonal/local ingredients | • Supports your community
• You can see the quality firsthand | • Search “bakery near me” on Google Maps or Yelp
• Ask friends/family for recommendations | | **Specialty Cake Shop** | • Signature desserts (e.g., French patisserie, vegan, gluten‑free)
• Unique flavor combinations | • Great for special occasions or dietary restrictions | • Look up “artisan cake shop” + city name
• Check Instagram or Facebook pages for photos & reviews | | **National Chains** | • Consistent quality & branding (e.g., Magnolia Bakery, Baked Goods Co.)
• Nationwide delivery via their own sites | • Reliable service & often offers promotions | • Visit chain website or use their mobile app | | **Online Delivery Platforms** | • Wide selection from multiple vendors (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates, Instacart) | • One‑stop shop; compare prices & delivery times | • Open the app, search “cake” or “dessert,” filter by rating | | **Grocery Store Delivery** | • Same‑day delivery from Whole Foods, Kroger, Safeway, etc.
• Often includes pre‑made cakes | • Convenient if you already shop there | • Use the store’s app or Amazon Fresh for same‑day delivery | | **Marketplace Sites** | • Etsy (handcrafted, custom cakes)
• Amazon (pre‑made, ready‑to‑deliver) | • Can find unique, artisanal options | • Search “custom cake” on Etsy; check seller ratings | ### Quick Tips for Ordering 1. **Check Reviews & Ratings** – Aim for at least 4 stars and read recent comments about freshness and customer service. 2. **Ask About Ingredients** – Especially if you have allergies or prefer organic/vegan options. 3. **Confirm Delivery Time & Fees** – Some platforms charge extra for rush or out‑of‑area deliveries. 4. **Look for Customization Options** – Many bakers allow you to choose frosting, fillings, and decorations. 5. **Order Early** – For holidays or birthdays, place your order at least 48–72 hours in advance to guarantee availability. ### Example Searches - *“Custom birthday cake Brooklyn”* → Local artisan shops in Brooklyn. - *“Vegan chocolate cake delivery Chicago”* → Specialty vegan bakeries or grocery delivery. - *“Same‑day cake delivery New York City”* → Grocery apps or local delivery services.
